name: Mid-Session Bootstrap
description: Detects ticket-id references in conversation mid-session and offers to retroactively pull the ticket plus set up per-ticket notes.

detectionPattern.label: Detection Pattern
detectionPattern.description: Regex pattern TPM uses to find ticket-id references in user turns. Default matches the conventional project-key-plus-number shape used by Jira and similar trackers (e.g., CMMS-5412, PROJ-123). Customize for teams with non-standard ticket formats; keep simple — over-broad patterns produce false positives on unrelated alphanumeric tokens.

autoOfferOnFirstMention.label: Auto-Offer On First Mention
autoOfferOnFirstMention.description: When on, TPM offers the bootstrap the FIRST time a matching ticket-id appears in a user turn during an unscoped session. When off, TPM waits for the user to explicitly ask. On is the typical flow for users who frequently start ad-hoc but realize partway through that the work is ticket-bound. Suppresses re-offers for the same ticket id in the same session.

bootstrapScope.label: Bootstrap Scope
bootstrapScope.description: Controls how much of the ticket-work-mode setup runs on bootstrap. full mirrors a fresh ticket-mode session — pulls the ticket from Jira, sets up per-ticket notes, surfaces any prior handoff, and scopes the remainder of the session to the ticket. notes-only sets up the notes file and pulls the ticket but does not enforce cross-ticket discipline for the rest of the session. lookup-only pulls the ticket for context but writes nothing and does not change session scope. Default full is the most useful when the user is committing to the ticket; the lighter scopes exist for I just want to look at this ticket briefly cases.

skipWhenTicketModeActive.label: Skip When Ticket Mode Active
skipWhenTicketModeActive.description: When on, mid-session bootstrap is silently skipped when mode.ticket-work is already enabled with a ticket id set — the user is already in a ticket session and the bootstrap would be redundant or scope-changing. When off, TPM offers the bootstrap even mid-ticket-session, which can surface switching to a different ticket gestures. On is the safer default.

skipWhenCdModeActive.label: Skip When CD Mode Active
skipWhenCdModeActive.description: When on, mid-session bootstrap is silently skipped when mode.cd is enabled — the user is in a directory-bound session and activating ticket-work behaviors mid-session would conflict with mode.cd's scope discipline. When off, mid-session bootstrap may offer the bootstrap even during a mode.cd session, which can create conflicting scope bindings. On is the safer default.

crossTicketBootstrap.label: Cross-Ticket Bootstrap
crossTicketBootstrap.description: Behavior when a SECOND distinct ticket id is mentioned in the same session after a previous bootstrap. ask prompts the user to confirm whether they want to switch session scope to the new ticket or just look at it briefly. switch immediately re-bootstraps to the new ticket and abandons the old one's scope. ignore silently skips the new mention. Default ask is the safest middle ground; tightens to switch for users who routinely hop between tickets.
